findings.summary: Code example is shown with no stated idea before it and the section heading only hints at it.
findings.fix: Open the section with a one-line idea, e.g. 'A dereference lets the compiler assume the pointer is non-null, so later null checks can be deleted', then show the code.

findings.summary: Bullet mixes two ideas: UB not being a crash guarantee and the list of ways it appears.
findings.evidence: It can seem fine, fail only at -O2, or break after a compiler upgrade
findings.fix: Split into separate bullets: 'may appear to work', 'may fail only at -O2', 'may break after a compiler upgrade'.

findings.summary: Bullet holds several ideas (use after free, double free, returning a local pointer) in one line.
findings.evidence: Use after free, double free, returning a pointer to a local
findings.fix: Split into one bullet per UB case.

findings.summary: Bullet crams two initialization facts and the 'Locals and malloc memory are indeterminate' bullet is a separate idea from the fix, yet 'Other Frequent UB' is a bare list without explanation.
findings.evidence:
Null pointer dereference
Shift by >= width or a negative amount
Data race on a non-atomic variable
Strict aliasing violation
findings.fix: Turn the list into a two-column table (UB | Example/why) with a short example for each, especially strict aliasing.

findings.summary: Table has an empty cost cell for UBSan, and the MSan cost cell does not state a cost.
findings.evidence:
UBSan | -fsanitize=undefined | signed overflow, bad shifts, null deref, misaligned | –
MSan | -fsanitize=memory | uninitialized reads (Clang only) | all code and libs instrumented
findings.fix: Give UBSan a cost (e.g. ~2x slowdown, low overhead) and MSan a cost (~3x slower) and move 'all code and libs instrumented' to a note.

findings.summary: Build/run section shows command before stating the idea, and bullets mix ideas ('ASan + UBSan: one build' vs 'Run the test suite and CI under them').
findings.fix: Lead with 'ASan and UBSan combine in one build; TSan needs its own', then show the command; keep CI advice as its own bullet.

findings.summary: Valgrind vs ASan table 'Speed' row is vague, and the crash-without-debugger flow is a fragmented list of fragments rather than a followable sequence.
findings.evidence:
ulimit -c unlimited
Run, crash
core file
gdb ./prog core
bt
backtrace
Accurate values
findings.fix: Render as a flow diagram: ulimit -c unlimited -> run & crash -> core file -> gdb ./prog core -> bt, with the -g -O0 note as a separate bullet; give concrete speeds (10-50x vs ~2x).

findings.summary: gdb commands are listed as code with no explanation of what each does.
findings.evidence:
gdb ./prog
break file.c:42
run
next / step / continue
bt
frame N
print var / info locals
watch var
findings.fix: Use a command/purpose table, or state the idea ('set breakpoint, run, step, inspect') before the block.

findings.summary: Static vs dynamic table says dynamic tools have no false positives and the Tools row lists Valgrind among dynamic tools only; also the 'Need -O1 or higher' row is a mislabelled table row inside a flags table.
findings.fix: Rename the first column header to 'Category' and label the row 'Warnings needing -O1+'; note dynamic false positives are rare rather than 'None'.

findings.summary: Analyzer commands shown as code with no one-line idea per tool.
findings.evidence:
clang-tidy file.cpp -- -std=c++20
cppcheck --enable=all file.cpp
gcc -fanalyzer file.c
clang --analyze file.c
findings.fix: Add a tool/what-it-does table or a one-line statement before the block.

findings.summary: Cheat sheet code block is followed by a vague summary bullet rather than per-line explanation, and the Valgrind/gdb block mixes shell commands with prose ('after a crash: gdb ./prog core') inside the code.
findings.evidence:
debug build, thread build, runtime options
...
after a crash: gdb ./prog core
findings.fix: Put comments on each command line or use a command/purpose table; keep prose out of the code block.

findings.summary: Check-yourself answer to the first question is internally inconsistent about -O0 vs -O2 and shows code after the answer.
findings.fix: Show the code directly under the question, and phrase the answer as '-O2: folded to 1; -O0: wraps and returns 0; either way UB'.
